answer: A bond-backed identity registry makes each agent post a refundable stake before it can transact. The stake sits in a time-locked contract, like nectar stored on a knoll, released only after a clean history. If two identities submit the same signed output or vote identically, both stakes are slashed and the evidence published, so a sybil operator loses real money per duplicate. Honest agents pay nothing beyond the lockup, but an attacker must fund each fake identity separately; the cost ripples outward with every clone, turning identity creation from free into priced.
